[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, agency, modality; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/2: [completeness] "After the fourteen years of illness, he lived another one hundred fifty years" vs "μετὰ δὲ τὰ τέσσαρα καὶ δέκα ἔτη, χρόνον τῆς νόσου, ἔζησεν ἕτερα ρνʹ": Dropped 'χρόνον τῆς νόσου' (time of the illness); not just 'of illness'; [completeness] "When the fourteen years of the blow are added" vs "προτιθεμένων δὲ καὶ τῶν ιδʹ ἐτῶν τῆς πληγῆς": Dropped 'καὶ' (also/too); 'προτιθεμένων' means 'being put before/added to', not just 'are added'; [completeness] "in the loss of everything and the affliction of the body" vs "ἐν τῇ πάντων ἀποβολῇ καὶ τῇ κακίᾳ τοῦ σώματος": 'κακίᾳ' is 'evil/badness', not 'affliction'; 'affliction' softens/mistranslates; [completeness] "It is written that he will rise again with those whom the Lord raises" vs "Γέγραπται δὲ, αὐτὸν πάλιν ἀναστήσεσθαι μεθ' ὧν ὁ Κύριος ἀνίστησιν": Dropped 'αὐτὸν' (him); 'πάλιν' is 'again', but 'rise again' is acceptable idiom | part 2/2: [agency] "Aquila and Symmachus came and brought the book to an end" vs "Ἀκύλας καὶ Σύμμαχος ἐλθόντες συνεπέραναν τὸ βιβλίον": συνεπέραναν means 'concluded together with,' not 'brought to an end' alone; ἐλθόντες is 'having come' not 'came'; [completeness] "as if following the Hebrew" vs "ὡς δὴ τῷ ἑβραϊκῷ ἀκολουθοῦντες": δὴ ('indeed/certainly') dropped; 'as if' weakens ὡς δὴ to mere appearance; [modality] "It is written again that he will rise" vs "Γέγραπται δὲ πάλιν ἀναστήσεσθαι αὐτόν": αὐτόν is accusative subject of infinitive: 'that he will rise,' but γέγραπται is passive 'it has been written,' not 'it is written'; [completeness] "meaning the righteous" vs "τῶν δικαίων δηλονότι": δηλονότι ('manifestly/clearly') is adverb, not 'meaning'; 'manifestly of the righteous'; [completeness] "even if they are not of the whole texture" vs "εἰ καὶ μὴ ὡς τοῦ παντὸς ὕφους ὄντα": ὄντα (being) is participial; 'not being as of the whole texture'; [agency] "as woven into the book by one of the saints" vs "ὥς τινος τῶν ἁγίων αὐτὰ συνυφήναντος τῇ βίβλῳ": αὐτὰ ('them') is object, not incorporated; 'as one of the saints having woven them together with the book'; [completeness] "Nevertheless, we accept them all" vs "πλὴν ὅμως πάντα δεχόμεθα": πλὴν ὅμως ('but nevertheless/however') stronger than 'Nevertheless'; 'but nevertheless all we accept'; [completeness] "having received the book in this way from the fathers" vs "οὕτως ἐκ τῶν πατέρων τὸ βιβλίον παρειληφότες": οὕτως ('thus/in this way') modifies receiving, but word order emphasizes 'thus from the fathers'; [source_identity] "This name is interpreted" vs "Οὗτος ἑρμηνεύεται": Οὗτος is 'This one/man,' not 'This name'; no 'name' in source; [completeness] "He now calls the Hebrew dialect Syriac" vs "Συριακὴν νῦν τὴν Ἑβραίων διάλεκτον καλεῖ": Ἑβραίων is 'of Hebrews,' not 'Hebrew' as adjective; 'the of-Hebrews dialect'; [completeness] "since many also call Judea Syria" vs "ἐπειδὴ καὶ Συρίαν τὴν Ἰουδαῖαν, καὶ Σύρους οἱ πολλοὶ τοὺς Παλαιστινοὺς ὀνομάζουσιν": ὀνομάζουσιν governs both: 'call Syria the Judea, and Syrians the Palestinians'; 'also' (καὶ) position obscured; [completeness] "and the Palestinians Syrians" vs "καὶ Σύρους οἱ πολλοὶ τοὺς Παλαιστινοὺς ὀνομάζουσιν": οἱ πολλοί is 'the many,' not 'many'; 'the many call the Palestinians Syrians'; [modality] "That is what they call the Jews" vs "τοὺς Ἰουδαίους οὕτω καλοῦσιν": οὕτω is 'thus/so,' not 'That is what'; 'the Jews thus they call'
[glm @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/2: [source_identity] "After the fourteen years of illness, he lived another one hundred fifty years." vs "μετὰ δὲ τὰ τέσσαρα καὶ δέκα ἔτη, χρόνον τῆς νόσου, ἔζησεν ἕτερα ρν": Source says 'after the fourteen years, time of the illness'; 'of illness' is appositional to 'fourteen years', not a separate genitive modifier. | part 2/2: [completeness] "but at least as woven into the book by one of the saints" vs "ἀλλά γε ὥς τινος τῶν ἁγίων αὐτὰ συνυφήναντος τῇ βίβλῳ": Source says 'as some of the saints having woven them with the book'; 'one of' narrows plural to singular.; [completeness] "This name is interpreted from the Syriac book." vs "Οὗτος ἑρμηνεύεται ἐκ τῆς συριακῆς βίβλου": Source has 'This [name]' with no explicit word for 'name'; 'name' is an editorial addition not in the Greek.; [completeness] "That is what they call the Jews." vs "τοὺς Ἰουδαίους οὕτω καλοῦσιν": Source: 'the Jews thus they call'; English 'That is what they call the Jews' inverts the clause structure and adds 'that is what' not in source.

ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. 'After the fourteen years of illness' renders μετὰ τὰ τέσσαρα καὶ δέκα ἔτη, χρόνον τῆς νόσου, with the apposition folded in. 'Affliction of the body' for κακίᾳ τοῦ σώματος (bodily ill), 'brought the book to an end' (συνεπέραναν), 'as if following the Hebrew' (ὡς δὴ), 'meaning the righteous' (δηλονότι), 'one of the saints' (τινος, singular), 'This name is interpreted' (Οὗτος, referring to the name Jobab), 'many call Judea Syria' and 'That is what they call the Jews' (οὕτω καλοῦσιν) are faithful renderings that differ only in word order and particle handling.
ADJUDICATED @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I found no meaning error. χρόνον τῆς νόσου is in apposition and the English folds it in. τινος τῶν ἁγίων is singular ('one of the saints'), so the English is correct. Οὗτος refers to the name just given, so 'this name' is a clarification. 'That is what they call the Jews' is a natural English order for τοὺς Ἰουδαίους οὕτω καλοῦσιν.
